purpose.heading: Stop fighting your tools. Start running the business.
body: Too many teams lose time every week to messy handoffs, endless spreadsheets, and apps that don’t match how people really work. Progress slows — not because the team isn’t trying, but because the tools get in the way.

Promptstack Technologies builds the software, automation, and digital systems that fix that. We make tools that fit your process, so your team can work faster, with fewer workarounds, and with a clear owner for every part.

hero.body: Promptstack Technologies is a software, automation, digital marketing, and Academy company. We help organisations run clearer processes today — and train the talent that will keep those systems alive tomorrow.

story.heading: Too many businesses are stuck between ambition and broken tools.
body: Leaders want modern systems. Teams want tools that match real work. Students want skills that open doors. Too often, those goals sit in three different rooms — with three different vendors, three timelines, and no shared owner.

Promptstack was built to close that gap. We design and ship websites, software, AI & automation, and growth systems that people can actually run — and through Academy we train students and aspiring tech professionals in web development, digital marketing, and AI.

vision.heading: A future where business processes feel light — and capability stays close to the people doing the work.
body: We believe the next era of business is not more software for its own sake. It is connected systems, practical automation, measurable growth, and people who know how to build and operate what they use.
Promptstack’s ecosystem is how we bring that closer: delivery for companies, training for talent, and a standard of work that prefers proof over slides.

howWeWin.heading: Win by shipping useful systems — and raising the people who can run them.
howWeWin.body: Our plan is simple and demanding: stay close to real constraints, deliver in reviewable slices, and grow talent that can keep the stack moving after go-live.

items.title: One connected stack
items.body: Software, automation, marketing, and Academy reinforce each other — so clients don’t buy four disconnected promises.

items.title: Clarity over theatre

items.title: Ship what people can run
items.body: Pretty screens without owners don’t count. We design for handover, ownership, and day-two reality.

items.title: Evidence over opinion
items.body: Demos, metrics, and finished work decide what stays. We optimise for outcomes you can point to.

items.title: Leave capability behind
items.body: Whether through project handover or Academy training, we want strength to remain on your side.

ceoWord.heading: The future we dreamed of should feel practical at work.

serviceItems.name: Software & websites
serviceItems.summary: Websites, apps, and tools built around how your team works.
serviceItems.body: We build company websites, client portals, and custom web apps your team can run day to day — matched to how work actually moves, not a template that almost fits.
serviceItems.detailBody: Need a clear company website, a client portal, or software that replaces messy spreadsheets? We design and ship it so your team can actually use it — clear pages and workflows, sensible permissions, and releases you can review before go-live.
serviceItems.problem: Your brand looks unclear online, or your team still runs critical work in spreadsheets and chat because no tool quite fits. Off-the-shelf software forces workarounds. A weak website loses trust before the first conversation.
details: Company websites and landing pages that explain what you do and convert interest
Web apps, client portals, and ops dashboards shaped to your real process
Discovery workshops to map the work before we propose screens
Iterative builds with demos, then handover and training so ownership stays with your team
Responsive design, SEO basics, and performance tuned for real visitors
Admin access, documentation, and training so you’re not locked to us forever

process.title: Discover
process.body: We map goals, audiences, content, and the workflows the site or app must support.

process.title: Design & plan
process.body: Information architecture, key screens, and a build sequence you can review before we code.

process.title: Build in slices
process.body: Weekly demos of working pages and features — feedback while change is still cheap.

process.title: Launch & hand over
process.body: Go-live checklist, training, docs, and named owners on your side.

modules.title: Company websites that convert
modules.body: Clear story, services, proof, and contact paths — built to load fast on mobile and desktop, with forms and analytics wired in.

modules.title: Client portals & web apps
modules.body: Login areas, dashboards, and tools that replace spreadsheet chaos — permissions, notifications, and flows that match how your team works.

modules.title: Maintainable delivery
modules.body: Clean structure, sensible CMS or admin where needed, and documentation so updates don’t require a rescue mission.

outcomes: A website or product customers and your team understand immediately
Fewer manual patches between tools and people
Clear ownership after launch — not a system only the vendor can touch
A foundation you can grow without rebuilding from zero
serviceItems.audience: Companies that need a professional website, a client-facing portal, or internal software that matches how work really gets done.

faqs.title: Do you rebuild from scratch or improve what we have?
faqs.body: Either. We’ll recommend the lighter path when an existing site or app can be fixed; we rebuild when the foundation can’t support the outcome you need.

faqs.title: Will our team be able to update content?
faqs.body: Yes when it matters. We set up editing paths and train the people who will own day-to-day updates.

faqs.title: How long does a typical project take?
faqs.body: A focused marketing site can move in weeks; portals and custom apps take longer depending on workflows and integrations. We lock a useful first win early.

serviceItems.imageAlt: Developer working late at a desk with code on multiple screens

serviceItems.name: AI & Automation
serviceItems.summary: Automate the repetitive steps that steal your week.
serviceItems.body: We find the handoffs, copy-paste loops, and approval piles worth fixing — then automate them with maintainable workflows, not demo theatre.
serviceItems.detailBody: We look for the grind that burns hours without adding judgment — re-keying, chasing approvals, status updates, document routing — and replace it with automations your team can understand and maintain. AI is used where it helps; reliable workflows win where they do.
serviceItems.problem: People copy data between tools, chase approvals in chat, and retype the same updates every day. Hours disappear into work that never needed a human — and errors creep in when someone is tired.
details: Process audit to spot high-ROI automation candidates
Workflow automation across forms, approvals, notifications, and handoffs
Practical AI assist where it reduces error or speeds decisions
Integrations between the tools you already use
Monitoring and playbooks so automations don’t become mysterious debts
Training so operators know what to check when something fails

process.title: Audit the grind
process.body: We sit with the people doing the work and list repeatable steps that cost time or create errors.

process.title: Prioritise ROI
process.body: We score candidates by impact vs effort and pick a first automation worth shipping soon.

process.title: Build & test
process.body: We implement, edge-case test, and put monitoring in place before you rely on it daily.

process.title: Hand over with playbooks
process.body: Docs, owners, and a simple runbook — so the automation stays yours.

modules.title: Ops & admin automation
modules.body: Approvals, reminders, data sync, document routing, and status updates that used to live in chat and spreadsheets.

modules.title: Practical AI assists
modules.body: Drafting, classification, extraction, and decision support — only where accuracy and review paths make sense.

modules.title: Reliable operations
modules.body: Alerts, logs, and fallbacks so a failed step doesn’t silently break the week.

outcomes: Hours back each week on tasks that used to drag
Fewer dropped handoffs and fewer copy-paste mistakes
Automations your team can explain and keep running
A clearer path from “we should automate this” to something live
serviceItems.audience: Operations, admin, and growth teams drowning in repeatable tasks that should already run themselves.

faqs.title: Do you only use AI?
faqs.body: No. Many wins are solid workflow automation. We add AI when it clearly reduces effort or error — not for the pitch deck.

faqs.title: Can you work with our existing tools?
faqs.body: Usually yes. We start with what you already use and only introduce new tools when they earn their place.

faqs.title: What if an automation breaks?
faqs.body: We design monitoring and a simple playbook so your team knows what to check — and we can support aftercare when you want it.

serviceItems.imageAlt: Human and robot hands shaking — partnership between people and automation

serviceItems.name: Digital Marketing
serviceItems.summary: Acquisition and content tied to numbers you can defend.
serviceItems.body: SEO, paid media, content, and analytics connected so attention turns into pipeline — with reporting operators can trust.
serviceItems.detailBody: We build growth systems, not disconnected campaigns. Channels, landing experiences, and reporting stay wired together so you can see what spent money, what converted, and what to do next.
serviceItems.problem: Ads, content, and SEO run in separate silos. Money goes out, leads come in unevenly, and nobody can clearly say what worked. Reporting looks busy but doesn’t help next week’s decisions.
details: Channel strategy across SEO, paid media, and content with clear priorities
Landing pages and funnels aligned to the offer and audience
Tracking and analytics that connect spend to leads and conversion
Content systems that support search and sales conversations
Campaign setup, optimisation, and creative iteration
Reporting your team can use week to week — not vanity metrics alone

process.title: Diagnose the funnel
process.body: We review offer, audience, channels, tracking, and where leads drop today.

process.title: Set the growth plan
process.body: Priorities, budget logic, and success metrics for the next useful period — not a fantasy annual roadmap.

process.title: Ship and measure
process.body: Launch pages, campaigns, and content with tracking in place from day one.

process.title: Optimise weekly
process.body: Review what moved, cut what didn’t, and double down with clear next actions.

modules.title: Acquisition systems
modules.body: SEO foundations, paid media structure, and campaigns aimed at qualified interest — not noise.

modules.title: Conversion paths
modules.body: Landing pages, offers, and follow-up flows that turn attention into conversations and leads.

modules.title: Measurement you can trust
modules.body: Clean tracking, dashboards, and weekly reporting tied to leads and revenue signals.

outcomes: Channels that support one clear growth plan
Spend tied to leads and conversions you can track
Weekly reporting your team can act on without a translator
A repeatable way to test offers instead of guessing
serviceItems.audience: Founders and marketing leads who want growth they can measure — not campaigns that look busy and stay opaque.

faqs.title: Do you run ads only, or full-funnel work?
faqs.body: We connect channels to landing experiences and tracking. Ads alone without a conversion path usually waste money.

faqs.title: Can you work with our existing website?
faqs.body: Yes. We’ll improve what converts and recommend rebuilds only when the current site blocks growth.

faqs.title: How do you report results?
faqs.body: Plain-language weekly or bi-weekly reporting: what we spent, what came in, what changed, and what we do next.

serviceItems.name: Academy
serviceItems.summary: Train for web development, digital marketing, and AI.
serviceItems.body: Promptstack Academy trains students and aspiring tech professionals in web development, digital marketing, and AI — through practical projects, not slide-only courses.
serviceItems.detailBody: Promptstack Academy is built for students and aspiring tech professionals who want job-ready skills. Choose a focused track — Web Development, Digital Marketing, or AI Training — learn by building, get mentored feedback, and leave with projects you can show employers.
serviceItems.problem: Many courses stop at theory and certificates. Graduates still can’t build a site, run a campaign, or apply AI to real tasks — so employers don’t trust the résumé.
details: Three focused tracks: Web Development, Digital Marketing, and AI Training
Project-based learning with mentored reviews
Portfolio-ready outputs you can show in interviews
Practical tools and workflows used in real delivery
Clear fees in FCFA — no vague “contact for pricing” games
Supportive cohort environment for students and career switchers

process.title: Choose your track
process.body: Pick Web Development, Digital Marketing, or AI Training based on the career path you want.

process.title: Learn by building
process.body: Lessons are tied to exercises and projects — not endless theory with no output.

process.title: Get reviewed
process.body: Mentors critique your work so you improve the way real teams improve: with feedback.

process.title: Show your proof
process.body: Finish with portfolio pieces and clearer language for applications and interviews.

modules.title: Who Academy is for
modules.body: Students, recent graduates, and aspiring tech professionals who want practical skills in web development, digital marketing, or AI — not another certificate with nothing to show.

modules.title: How classes run
modules.body: Structured lessons, hands-on practice, project milestones, and mentor feedback. You leave with work products, not only notes.

modules.title: What “done” looks like
modules.body: Completed projects, a clearer skill story for your CV, and confidence using the tools of your track.

Better judgment on when to trust or override AI output
A mini-project that proves applied AI skill

outcomes: Job-ready practice in web development, digital marketing, or AI
Finished projects that strengthen applications and interviews
Mentored feedback instead of learning alone in silence
A clearer story about what you can actually do
serviceItems.audience: Students and aspiring tech professionals who want practical training in web development, digital marketing, or AI.

faqs.title: Who can join Academy?
faqs.body: Students, recent graduates, and aspiring tech professionals. No need to already work at a company — motivation and consistency matter most.

faqs.title: Are the fees per course?
faqs.body: Yes. Web Development is 250,000 FCFA, Digital Marketing is 250,000 FCFA, and AI Training is 100,000 FCFA.

faqs.title: Do I get a certificate?
faqs.body: You’ll get recognition for completion — but the priority is portfolio proof and skills you can demonstrate, not a paper certificate alone.

faqs.title: Can I take more than one track?
faqs.body: Yes. Many learners start with one track, then add another. We’ll help you sequence them if you’re unsure.

faqs.title: Is this online or in person?
faqs.body: Ask us for the current cohort format (in-person, online, or hybrid) and schedule for your preferred track.

portfolioItems.title: Finance Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A trust-first web presence for a finance brand that needed to look institutional online without slowing day-to-day content updates.
portfolioItems.challenge: The previous site felt dated, buried key products, and gave little confidence to first-time visitors comparing providers. Leadership needed a clearer story, stronger visual hierarchy, and a structure marketing could maintain.
portfolioItems.role: Promptstack led discovery, information architecture, UI design, and front-end build — then handed over an editable structure with training so the client team could publish without breaking the layout.
portfolioItems.outcome: A clearer finance narrative on first scroll, faster paths to contact, and an owned publishing workflow — so the website supports sales conversations instead of apologising for itself.

portfolioItems.title: Photography Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A portfolio site built to sell bookings — not just display pretty pictures.
portfolioItems.challenge: Strong imagery was trapped in a weak layout: slow galleries, unclear packages, and no confident path from admiration to enquiry.
portfolioItems.role: We redesigned the visual system, curated project storytelling, and wired booking/enquiry flows so the studio’s best work does commercial work.
portfolioItems.outcome: Visitors understand the offer in seconds, galleries feel premium on mobile, and enquiries arrive with clearer intent.

portfolioItems.title: Makeup Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A beauty brand site centred on lookbooks, services, and booking interest.
portfolioItems.challenge: Visual brand strength was not translating into clear service packages or enquiries.
portfolioItems.role: Design and build of a conversion-oriented beauty web presence with gallery and CTA structure.
portfolioItems.outcome: Clearer packaging online and a more confident path from inspiration to contact.

portfolioItems.title: Business Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A business site designed for credibility with procurement-minded buyers.
portfolioItems.challenge: Generic brochure pages failed to explain process, proof, or next steps. Sales still had to re-explain the company on every first call.
portfolioItems.role: We rebuilt the narrative around diagnose → define → deliver, added proof sections, and made CTAs match how their sales team actually qualifies leads.
portfolioItems.outcome: Prospects arrive on calls already oriented — less time spent defending the brand, more time scoping the engagement.

portfolioItems.title: Crypto Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A crypto/fintech marketing UI that balances energy with enough structure for serious visitors.
portfolioItems.challenge: Hype-heavy visuals without explainer hierarchy made the offer feel risky rather than credible.
portfolioItems.role: UI/UX design for product story, feature blocks, and trust-oriented CTAs.
portfolioItems.outcome: A more institutional first impression while keeping the category’s visual energy.

portfolioItems.title: Beauty Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A beauty services website focused on treatments, proof, and bookings.
portfolioItems.challenge: Service menus were hard to scan; mobile users struggled to find how to book.
portfolioItems.role: Redesign of service taxonomy, proof modules, and booking CTAs.
portfolioItems.outcome: Faster understanding of offerings and a shorter path to book or enquire.

portfolioItems.title: HomeCare Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A home-care web presence that explains services, coverage, and how to request help.
portfolioItems.challenge: Families needed reassurance and clarity; the old site looked informal and incomplete.
portfolioItems.role: Trust-led redesign with service clarity and request flows.
portfolioItems.outcome: A calmer, more trustworthy first visit — especially on mobile.

portfolioItems.title: Temporary Number
portfolioItems.summary: A product-facing web experience for a temporary-number concept: clear value proposition, trust, and signup intent.
portfolioItems.challenge: Privacy and utility products fail when the landing page cannot explain the offer in one screen or build enough trust to try.
portfolioItems.role: Promptstack designed and built the product narrative, feature explanation, and conversion path as a showcase of product marketing craft.
portfolioItems.outcome: A crisp product story that demonstrates how Promptstack ships product interfaces — not only brochure sites.

portfolioItems.title: Fashion Portfolio Design
portfolioItems.summary: A fashion portfolio site for showcasing collections with editorial pacing.
portfolioItems.challenge: Imagery needed space to breathe without losing navigation or contact access.
portfolioItems.role: Editorial web design and portfolio storytelling.
portfolioItems.outcome: A portfolio that feels like a lookbook and still drives professional enquiries.

portfolioItems.title: HomeCare Web Design
portfolioItems.summary: A second home-care design direction exploring clearer packaging and visual trust.
portfolioItems.challenge: Need for a stronger visual system and simpler request path.
portfolioItems.role: Alternate design system and page structure for home-care conversion.
portfolioItems.outcome: A refined option set for choosing the direction that best matched brand voice.

portfolioItems.title: Lady Care Design
portfolioItems.summary: A wellness brand site with calm hierarchy and clear next steps.
portfolioItems.challenge: Soft branding without structure left visitors unsure what to do next.
portfolioItems.role: Design of brand web pages balancing care aesthetics with conversion.
portfolioItems.outcome: A composed digital presence that invites contact without visual noise.

portfolioItems.title: Body Trimmer Design
portfolioItems.summary: Product marketing pages for a body-care device with benefit-led storytelling.
portfolioItems.challenge: Specs alone did not sell; benefits and trust needed a clearer narrative.
portfolioItems.role: Product landing design emphasising benefits, proof, and purchase/interest CTAs.
portfolioItems.outcome: A landing pattern ready for campaigns and retailer handoff.

portfolioItems.title: Fashion Brand Design
portfolioItems.summary: Brand website for a fashion label needing stronger identity online.

posts.title: Diagnose before you build: why most digital projects fail in week one
posts.excerpt: Buying software or a redesign without naming the bottleneck is how companies fund activity instead of outcomes. Here is the diagnostic discipline Promptstack uses before any build.
posts.body:
Most failed digital projects do not fail in the code. They fail in the brief.

A company decides it “needs a website”, “needs a CRM”, or “needs automation”. A vendor quotes. Screens appear. Three months later the team still works in WhatsApp and spreadsheets — and the new system becomes another tab nobody opens.

The missing step is diagnosis.

What we mean by diagnose
Before we propose tools, we sit with the people who do the work and answer four questions in plain language:

1. Where does time actually disappear each week?
2. Which handoff creates the most rework or blame?
3. What does “better” look like in 30–60 days — not in a three-year roadmap?
4. Who will own the system after go-live?

If those answers are vague, any build will be vague.

A useful first win beats a fantasy architecture
Corporate buyers sometimes ask for a full platform on day one. That ambition is fine — but the first release should still protect one measurable win: fewer missed follow-ups, faster membership renewals, cleaner invoicing, a site that qualifies leads properly.

Promptstack’s engagement model is deliberate: diagnose → define → deliver → transfer ownership. The first phase exists to stop you paying for the wrong system.

What this means for your next RFP
Ask every vendor — including us — to show how they will discover the bottleneck before they sell you screens. If the proposal jumps straight to features, you are buying a catalogue, not a transformation.

posts.title: Go-live is not the finish line: transferring ownership that sticks
posts.excerpt: The most expensive systems are the ones only the vendor can touch. Ownership maps, training, and admin design decide whether your investment compounds or decays.
posts.body:
Launch day feels like success. Screenshots go into the WhatsApp group. Leadership is relieved. Then someone leaves, a password is lost, and the “new system” quietly returns to Excel.

That pattern is not a people problem first. It is a delivery design problem.

Ownership is a deliverable
At Promptstack we treat handover as part of the product:

• Named owners for content, operations, and technical access
• Admin paths that match how your team actually updates work
• Short training focused on the weekly jobs — not a 40-page PDF nobody reads
• Documentation that answers “what breaks if I change this?”

Why corporates should care
When you buy a ₣2M–₣10M engagement, you are buying continuity. A portal, membership workflow, or automation stack that only the agency can modify becomes a hostage situation — or a silent failure.

Questions to ask before you sign
• Who on our side will be able to publish, approve, and report without calling the vendor?
• What happens in month four when a campaign needs a new landing page?
• Which access and environments are documented?

If the proposal cannot answer those, you are renting a demo, not buying an operating capability.

posts.title: Beyond the brochure website: when your site should become an operating surface
posts.excerpt: A pretty homepage is not a growth system. Here is how to tell whether you need a brochure, a portal, or a connected stack — and how to budget accordingly.
posts.body:
Many organisations still buy websites as if they were printed brochures with a contact form. That can be enough — until membership renewals, event registration, invoicing, partner portals, or sales follow-up become the real constraint.

Three levels of digital maturity
1. Brochure presence — brand, services, proof, contact. Useful when buyers only need trust and a conversation starter.
2. Operating website — applications, bookings, content workflows, basic CRM handoff. Useful when the website is part of how work gets done.
3. Connected stack — website + CRM + email automation + admin + integrations. Useful when revenue or membership depends on reliable digital operations.

Most “we need a new website” requests are secretly level 2 or 3 problems wearing level 1 language.

How Promptstack scopes this
We start with the bottleneck, not the template. If your team loses renewals in inboxes, a redesign alone will not fix it. If your brand looks outdated but operations are fine, a strong marketing site may be the right first win.

Budget honesty
Level 1 work competes on taste and speed. Level 2–3 work competes on process design, integrations, and ownership. That is why corporate engagements look different from ₣100k–₣300k brochure projects — and why the brief should say so out loud.

posts.title: Automation that pays for itself: pick the boring bottlenecks first
posts.excerpt: AI demos are exciting. Repeatable handoffs, reminders, and data entry are where automation usually returns money. A practical way to prioritise.
posts.body:
Every leadership meeting has a slide about AI. Fewer meetings have a list of the five weekly tasks that burn the most staff hours.

Start with volume and pain
Good automation candidates share traits:

• They happen often (weekly or daily)
• They follow rules more than judgement
• Errors are expensive or embarrassing
• Someone already “owns” them in a messy way (spreadsheet heroics)

Examples we see often: lead routing, membership reminders, invoice status updates, report compilation, onboarding checklists, content approvals.

Resist theatre
A chatbot that cannot update your CRM is theatre. A workflow that moves a qualified enquiry from form → owner → follow-up with an audit trail is operations.

How we run automation engagements
1. Map the current path with the people who live it
2. Measure time / error cost on the worst two steps
3. Ship a thin automation slice with owners and monitoring
4. Only then expand

If a vendor sells you a platform tour before they can name your bottleneck in one sentence, pause.

posts.title: Marketing that connects to pipeline — not just impressions
posts.excerpt: Digital marketing earns trust when campaigns, content, and CRM follow-up share one path. Here is the minimum stack Promptstack insists on before scaling spend.
posts.body:
Spending on ads or content without a clean path to conversation is how budgets evaporate.

The minimum connected path
Before scaling acquisition, we want:

• A site (or landing) that states offer, proof, and next step clearly
• Forms that capture enough context for sales — not just an email
• Routing to a named owner with a response SLA
• Basic attribution: which campaign or page started the conversation
• A follow-up sequence that does not depend on one person’s memory

Content is a sales asset
An empty blog undermines a company that sells digital marketing. A few excellent articles that teach how you think — diagnosis, ownership, measurement — do more for corporate credibility than twenty thin posts.

What “good” looks like in 90 days
Not vanity metrics alone. Look for: qualified conversations booked, faster response times, clearer campaign ROI, and sales feedback that leads arrive oriented.

Promptstack builds marketing systems the same way we build software: diagnose the constraint, ship a useful slice, transfer ownership, then scale what works.

legal.title: Privacy Policy
legal.body:
Last updated: 5 October 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Promptstack Technologies (“Promptstack”, “we”, “us”, or “our”) collects, uses, stores, shares, and protects personal data when you visit promptstacktechnologies.com (the “Site”), contact us, book a discovery call, subscribe to updates, apply for a role, or otherwise interact with our services.

We designed this notice to meet expectations under major international frameworks, including the EU/UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR / UK GDPR), the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA (CCPA/CPRA), Cameroon’s Law No. 2010/012 relating to cybersecurity and cybercrime (personal data provisions), and related ePrivacy / cookie rules. Where local law grants you stronger rights, those rights apply.


1. Who is the data controller?

Promptstack Technologies is the controller of personal data processed through this Site and our related business communications.

Promptstack Technologies
Bonapriso, Douala, Cameroon
Email: hello@promptstacktechnologies.com
Phone: +237 674 047 453

Privacy requests: hello@promptstacktechnologies.com (subject line: “Privacy Request”).


2. Scope

This Policy covers personal data processed via:
• the marketing Site and forms (contact, newsletter, product interest, job applications);
• discovery-call booking and related scheduling / video tools;
• first-party analytics used to understand Site usage;
• email and operational communications about enquiries and projects.

It does not replace contracts we may sign with clients for delivery work. Client project processing is governed by the relevant service agreement and, where required, a data processing addendum.


3. Personal data we collect

Depending on how you interact with us, we may process:

A. Identity and contact data
Name, email address, phone number, company or role (if you provide it), and message content.

B. Enquiry and commercial data
Subject of your request, service interest, Academy interest, project details you share, and follow-up notes needed to respond.

C. Booking data
Preferred meeting time, timezone, and meeting metadata created when scheduling a discovery call (for example via Zoom or similar).

D. Application data
CV/résumé content, portfolio links, and answers you submit for careers / internships.

E. Newsletter data
Email address and your marketing consent status / timestamp.

F. Technical and usage data
IP address (as received by our servers/hosting), browser type, device/approximate locale, pages viewed, referrer, timestamps, and anonymous or pseudonymous visitor/session identifiers stored in your browser (localStorage / sessionStorage) when analytics is allowed.

G. Cookie and preference data
Locale preference cookie, admin session cookie (staff only), and your cookie/analytics consent choice.

We do not intentionally collect special-category data (e.g. health, biometrics, political opinions) through this Site. Please do not include such information in free-text fields unless we have expressly asked for it under a lawful basis.


4. How we collect data

• Directly from you (forms, email, phone, WhatsApp, meetings).
• Automatically when you use the Site (server logs, necessary cookies, and — only with consent where required — analytics identifiers).
• From service providers that help us operate the Site (hosting, email delivery, meeting tools), limited to what is needed to provide the service.


5. Purposes and legal bases (GDPR / UK GDPR)

We process personal data for the following purposes. Where GDPR/UK GDPR applies, the corresponding legal bases are:

Purpose | Legal basis
Respond to contact, Academy, and product-interest enquiries | Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)) to run our business and reply to you; or contract steps (Art. 6(1)(b)) where you request a proposal
Schedule and run discovery calls | Contract steps / legitimate interests
Send newsletter / marketing emails | Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)); you may withdraw anytime
Recruitment and internship applications | Legitimate interests and/or contract steps; consent where we ask for optional data
Operate, secure, and maintain the Site | Legitimate interests; legal obligation where applicable
Measure Site traffic and improve content (analytics) | Consent where required by ePrivacy/GDPR; otherwise legitimate interests for strictly aggregated, privacy-preserving measurement if permitted
Comply with law, prevent abuse, and establish/defend legal claims | Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)) and/or legitimate interests

Where we rely on legitimate interests, we balance those interests against your rights and expectations. You may object as described in Section 10.


6. Cookies, local storage, and similar technologies

We use:

• Strictly necessary cookies — e.g. language/locale (pst_locale) and authenticated admin session (pst_admin_session) for staff. These are required for basic Site function or security.
• Preference storage — your cookie/analytics choice (stored locally in your browser).
• Analytics storage (optional) — pseudonymous visitor and session IDs in localStorage / sessionStorage used only if you accept analytics/cookies. These help us count visits and popular pages. They are not used to sell your data or build advertising profiles for third parties.

Details are in our Cookie Policy. Non-essential analytics runs only after you accept via our cookie banner (or equivalent preference control).


7. Who we share data with

We do not sell personal information. We share data only with:

• Service providers (processors) acting on our instructions, such as:
  – Website hosting / edge delivery (e.g. Vercel);
  – Email delivery / mailbox (e.g. Zoho SMTP / Zoho Mail);
  – Analytics persistence (e.g. Upstash Redis) for aggregated visitor metrics;
  – Video / scheduling tools for discovery calls (e.g. Zoom);
  – Messaging channels you choose to contact us on (e.g. WhatsApp / Meta), which process data under their own terms when you use their apps.
• Professional advisers (legal, accounting) under confidentiality where needed.
• Authorities when required by applicable law or to protect rights, safety, and security.

We require processors to implement appropriate security and use data only for contracted purposes.


8. International transfers

We are based in Cameroon. Providers may process data in the EU, UK, United States, or other countries. Where GDPR/UK GDPR applies to a transfer, we use appropriate safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), provider DPAs, and transfer impact assessments where required, or rely on an adequacy decision when available.


9. Retention

We keep personal data only as long as needed for the purposes above, then delete or anonymise it, unless a longer period is required by law.

Typical periods (may be shorter or longer if justified):
• Contact / enquiry records: up to 24 months after last meaningful interaction
• Newsletter: until you unsubscribe or we suppress the address
• Booking records: up to 24 months
• Job applications: typically up to 12 months after the process ends (unless you ask us to keep a talent profile longer)
• Analytics events: rolling operational window (commonly up to 13 months) in aggregated or pseudonymous form
• Security / abuse logs: as needed for security and legal claims

You may request earlier deletion subject to legal exceptions (see Section 10).


10. Your rights

Depending on your location, you may have some or all of the following rights:

Under GDPR / UK GDPR / similar laws:
• Access your personal data
• Rectify inaccurate data
• Erase data (“right to be forgotten”) in certain cases
• Restrict or object to processing
• Data portability (for data you provided, where processing is consent- or contract-based and automated)
• Withdraw consent at any time (without affecting prior lawful processing)
• Lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (for example your local EU/EEA DPA, the UK ICO, or the competent Cameroonian authority)

Under CCPA/CPRA (if you are a California resident):
• Know / access categories and specific pieces of personal information collected
• Delete personal information (with exceptions)
• Correct inaccurate personal information
• Opt out of “sale” or “sharing” for cross-context behavioural advertising — we do not sell personal information and do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising
• Limit use of sensitive personal information (we do not seek sensitive PI via this Site)
• Non-discrimination for exercising privacy rights

To exercise rights, email hello@promptstacktechnologies.com with “Privacy Request” and enough detail to verify your identity and locate your data. We will respond within the timeframe required by applicable law (generally 30 days under GDPR, 45 days under CCPA, subject to permitted extensions).


11. Children’s privacy

The Site is directed to businesses and adults. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 16 (or under 13 where COPPA applies). If you believe a child provided data, contact us and we will delete it.


12. Security

We implement technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, including HTTPS, access controls for admin tools, least-privilege provider access, and staff need-to-know handling of enquiry data. No method of transmission or storage is 100% secure; please avoid sending passwords or highly sensitive secrets through website forms.


13. Automated decision-making

We do not use automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects about you based on Site data.


14. Third-party links and social platforms

The Site may link to LinkedIn, TikTok, or other third-party sites. Their privacy practices are governed by their own policies. If you contact us via WhatsApp or social DMs, those platforms also process your data.


15. Changes to this Policy

We may update this Policy to reflect legal, technical, or business changes. The “Last updated” date will change when we do. Material changes affecting your rights will be highlighted on the Site or communicated where required.


16. Contact

Questions or requests about this Privacy Policy:

Phone: +237 674 047 453

legal.title: Cookie Policy
legal.body:
Last updated: 5 October 2026

This Cookie Policy explains how Promptstack Technologies (“we”, “us”) uses cookies and similar technologies on promptstacktechnologies.com. It should be read with our Privacy Policy.


1. What are cookies and similar technologies?

Cookies are small text files stored on your device. Similar technologies include localStorage, sessionStorage, pixels, and scripts that store or read identifiers in your browser.

We use:
• HTTP cookies for a few essential Site functions;
• browser storage for analytics identifiers (only when you consent) and for remembering your cookie preference.


2. How we ask for consent

When you first visit (or after preferences expire/reset), we show a cookie banner. You can:
• Accept all — enables optional analytics measurement in addition to essential cookies;
• Essential only — we only use technologies required for the Site to work (and security).

You can change your mind later by clearing site data for this domain in your browser, which will prompt the banner again, or by contacting hello@promptstacktechnologies.com.


3. Categories we use

A. Strictly necessary
Required for core functionality, security, or to store your consent choice. These do not require consent under most ePrivacy regimes, but we still disclose them.

B. Preferences / functional
Remember language/locale so the Site displays in your chosen language.

C. Analytics / performance (optional)
Help us understand which pages are visited so we can improve content and reliability. These run only if you Accept all.


4. Technologies currently in use

Name / key | Type | Purpose | Duration | Category
pst_locale | Cookie | Stores language preference (en/fr) | Session / as configured by the Site | Necessary / functional
pst_admin_session | Cookie | Authenticates CMS/admin users (staff only) | Session / short-lived auth window | Strictly necessary (staff)
pst_cookie_consent | localStorage | Stores your cookie/analytics choice | Until cleared | Necessary (consent record)
pst_visitor | localStorage | Pseudonymous visitor ID for first-party analytics | Until cleared | Analytics (consent required)
pst_session | sessionStorage | Pseudonymous session ID for analytics | Browser session | Analytics (consent required)

Server logs on our hosting provider may also record technical request data (IP, user agent, URL, time) as part of operating a secure website. That processing is described in the Privacy Policy.


5. Third parties

Optional analytics events are sent to our own API and may be stored with infrastructure providers (for example Upstash Redis) acting as processors. We do not use third-party advertising cookies on the Site at this time.

If we later add advertising or third-party marketing tags, we will update this Policy and request consent before activating them where required.


6. Managing cookies in your browser

Most browsers let you block or delete cookies via settings. Blocking strictly necessary cookies may break login (admin) or language features.

Browser guides (external):
• Chrome — Settings → Privacy and security → Cookies
• Firefox — Settings → Privacy & Security
• Safari — Preferences → Privacy
• Edge — Settings → Cookies and site permissions


7. Do Not Track / Global Privacy Control

Where legally required, we honour browser opt-out signals for sale/sharing of personal information. We do not sell personal information. Analytics remains off unless you accept optional cookies.


8. Updates

We may update this Cookie Policy when our technologies or legal requirements change. The “Last updated” date will reflect the latest version.


9. Contact

Promptstack Technologies
Bonapriso, Douala, Cameroon
hello@promptstacktechnologies.com

legal.title: Acceptable Use Policy
legal.body:
Last updated: 5 October 2026

This Acceptable Use Policy (“AUP”) sets rules for using promptstacktechnologies.com and related Promptstack Technologies online services (forms, booking, newsletter, careers submissions). It complements our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.


1. Allowed use

You may use the Site to learn about Promptstack, contact us, book discovery calls, apply for roles, and access publicly available materials in good faith.


2. Prohibited use

You must not:

Security and abuse
• Attempt to gain unauthorised access to systems, accounts, or data
• Probe, scan, or test vulnerability except with our prior written authorisation
• Introduce malware, ransomware, or harmful code
• Overwhelm infrastructure (DDoS, unreasonable automated load)

Fraud and deception
• Impersonate any person or entity
• Submit false identity or contact details to deceive us or others
• Phish, social-engineer, or harvest information from the Site unlawfully

Content and communications
• Upload or transmit unlawful, harassing, hateful, or pornographic content
• Infringe intellectual property, privacy, or publicity rights
• Spam forms or send bulk unsolicited messages through Site channels

Automated access
• Scrape the Site at a volume or frequency that degrades service, or circumvent rate limits / robots rules, without permission
• Use bots to flood bookings or applications

Illegal activity
• Use the Site in connection with any activity that violates Cameroonian law, applicable international sanctions, export controls, or the laws of your jurisdiction


3. Academy and client communications

When corresponding about Academy programmes or client work, you must not share credentials belonging to others, or content you are not authorised to disclose.


4. Enforcement

We may investigate suspected violations, remove content, block access, cancel bookings, and report matters to authorities where appropriate. We may cooperate with lawful investigations.


5. Reporting

Report suspected abuse to hello@promptstacktechnologies.com with subject “Abuse Report”.


6. Changes

We may update this AUP. Continued use of the Site after updates constitutes acceptance where permitted by law.


7. Contact

Promptstack Technologies
Bonapriso, Douala, Cameroon
hello@promptstacktechnologies.com
